exception.reason: UCR offers genuine related study in mathematical modelling, signals and feedback, robotics, computing, materials and energy assessment. The strongest feasible24course combination was tested using those subjects and product design. It remains organised around general mathematical/computational methods and sustainable-technology appraisal rather than sustained aircraft or spacecraft physical design, where aerodynamics, structural loads, propulsion and vehicle dynamics must be integrated and tested. Further environmental, resource and infrastructure courses do not supply that missing organising inquiry. A transparent limitation or an assumed aerospace project would not repair this programme-level gap. No sufficiently close UCR programme is therefore presented.

All23nonPPDcontributions were assessed from actual selected evidence; description-onlyAdvancedCalculus,ReinforcementLearning andRenewableSystemDesign receive full consideration within their stated scope. They do not establish a sustained aerodynamic-flow,lightweight-structure,propulsion andflight/orbital-dynamics design inquiry. Additional coastal/ecological infrastructure,geophysical surveying andresource-recovery laboratory work were examined rather than excluded by title. No-match follows academic programme-level assessment, not missing offerings,degree-name equivalence,a professional-licence requirement or unavailable external evidence.

audience.programmeDescription: Aerospace Engineering at Delft combines mathematics and physics with aerodynamics, structures, materials, propulsion, flight and space systems. Design projects, experiments, a minor and a final team design exercise connect these subjects.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in mathematical systems, computing, robotics and sustainable technology. The available courses do not form a sufficiently close programme centred on aircraft and spacecraft physical design, so only the verified external curriculum is shown.

curriculum.limitation: The 180-EC curriculum includes a 30-EC minor and a compulsory 15-EC team design exercise. Course-entry, minor approval and final-project registration conditions apply.
